Subject: Pilot econ hedge bounds — batching/quantization split

Hi Riley —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. We sketched a few approaches on how to structure the pilot economics so you can both protect performance and realize immediate unit-cost savings. Before we lock anything into a one-pager, can you confirm which of the two high-level hedging philosophies CloudLedger prefers?

Option A — Cache/Batch-first (lower latency priority):
- Aggressive prefix/KV caching for chat paths
- Larger batch windows for async inference (non-interactive flows)
- Quantization applied selectively to background jobs

Option B — Quantization-first (cost-first, slightly higher tail latency):
- Apply int8/4 quantized model variants for most LLM traffic
- Keep caching conservative to protect tail-latency-sensitive routes
- Reserve batching for bulk inference only

Our thought: for a short 8-week pilot, many customers land on a blended approach (roughly 65/35 batching+cache / quantization), then tier the split by route (chat vs async pipelines). That lets you show cost wins quickly while keeping a safety margin for SLA-sensitive endpoints.

If you prefer, we can put numbers behind both approaches — modeled USD per 100M tokens under your assumed traffic mix. Also: who should I include from your procurement/technical ops side?

Next steps we propose:
1) We produce a two-page costing sketch (per-100M token model for A/B).
2) Marcus will draft recommended quantization profiles and expected quality delta by route.
3) Joint call next week to finalize pilot commit and credit sizing.

Attaching a short outline in the Drive link below; will follow up with Marcus' technical matrix.

Thanks,

Thanks Sofia — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed internally. A couple of clarifying questions before we ask legal/procurement to start: 

1) How do the credits apply if we want to run a mixed fleet (hosted + private Dedicated nodes)? Is the credit consumption per-token consistent across environments or do you model different unit costs?
2) For the modeled numbers, can you show both (a) end-to-end cost including network/GPU premium for Dedicated and (b) hosted-only? Procurement will want both views.
3) On quantization: what's the expected quality delta on our NLU intent extraction flows for int8 vs int4? We need an ops-safe threshold — <1% intent regression ideally.

I'll loop in Alex (cc'd) from procurement — Alex can drive the contract path once we see the sketches. Also add any compliance notes you have on data residency for private nodes (we run EU-sensitive workloads on some customers).

Hi Riley —

Following up with the technical breakdown you asked for. I'm attaching two artifacts: a quant recommendation matrix (by model family and route) and a short batch-savings scenarios PDF with per-100M token numbers under three traffic mixes. See attachments: quant-recommendation-matrix.xlsx; batching-savings-scenarios.pdf

Key assumptions (summary):
- Baseline model: Redwood-rlm-13B (float16)
- Quantized variants: int8 (safe for most NLU/chat); int4 (aggressive, larger latency variance)
- KV cache hit assumption for chat routes: conservative 25% (pilot stage) up to 45% if warm prefixes are established
- Typical batch window used for async jobs in our scenarios: 150–300ms (lower bound) which favors higher throughput with modest added latency

Per-100M token modeled costs (summary bullets — see PDF for full table):
- Hosted float16 baseline: $18.2 per 100M tokens
- Hosted + int8 variant (mixed traffic): $10.4 per 100M tokens (~43% savings)
- Hosted + int4 aggressive: $6.9 per 100M tokens (~62% savings) but expected quality regression risk on sensitive NLU tasks
- Dedicated (with hardware premium + reserved capacity): add 18–28% to hosted baseline unless you commit to sustained throughput (>500K tokens/min); with commits we push the premium down to ~8–12%

Recommendations for CloudLedger pilot:
1) Start with blended split: 60% cache+batch optimization on chat routes + int8 for async/backfill pipelines. That hits ~45% blended savings in modeled numbers and keeps <1% intent regression risk per our evals on similar customers.
2) Hold a 15% safety cushion in credits for burst/ops headroom (we can structure this as reserve credits that are refundable if unused at end of pilot).
3) If procurement needs a hosted vs dedicated line-item, we can model both in the one-pager; the PDF shows both hosted-only and hosted+dedicated columns.

Notes on residency/compliance: private Dedicated nodes (VPC) keep logs and KV cache on your VPC. We provide KMS integrations for key management and audit logs exported to your SIEM. I'll add a short compliance note into the Drive folder.

-----Attachments-----
quant-recommendation-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet: model family, route, quality delta estimate)
batching-savings-scenarios.pdf (pdf: three traffic mixes, per-100M token cost)

Happy to walk through any row in the spreadsheet — happy to join a call with Alex and your engineers.
